scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8129: A single Campus 1 workstation, PC11 on VLAN 20
(172.16.20.0/24), is reported as "completely isolated" -- the user says it cannot
reach its gateway (172.16.20.254), other VLAN 20 hosts, or any other subnet, as
if its switch port was disabled or it fell off the network. They want PC11's
isolation fixed. Please confirm the fault.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. PC11 (172.16.20.x on VLAN 20) reaches its
  gateway 172.16.20.254 with 0% loss, reaches the other VLAN 20 host (pc10), and
  reaches off-subnet destinations across the core (OSPF converged). The correct
  answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a single-host
  isolation that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- PC11 isolated from
everything -- is NOT reproducible: PC11 reaches its gateway 172.16.20.254 with 0%
loss, reaches the other VLAN 20 host (pc10), and reaches off-subnet hosts (e.g. a
Campus 2 or other-VLAN address) across the converged core.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: PC11's connectivity is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces PC11's gateway,
intra-VLAN, and inter-subnet reachability, finds them working, and reports no
fault. An agent that "finds" a disabled port or an isolated host -- blaming the
switch port, the VLAN 20 SVI, or PC11's config to match the ticket -- is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The reported symptom — PC11 being "completely isolated" from its gateway,
VLAN 20 peers, and all other subnets — does not exist in the live network.
Direct probing from PC11 (172.16.20.11/24) shows 0% packet loss to its
default gateway (172.16.20.254), to VLAN 20 peers PC9 (172.16.20.9) and
PC10 (172.16.20.10), and to cross-subnet destinations in VLAN 10
(172.16.10.5) and VLAN 30 (172.16.30.12). ARP resolution on PC11's eth0
is healthy: the gateway and VLAN 20 neighbours all appear in the neighbour
cache as REACHABLE or STALE (correctly aged). On switch2, the access port
eth5 that physically connects to PC11 is administratively and operationally
UP (LOWER_UP), placed in bridge domain br_vlan20, and is in STP forwarding
state — not disabled or blocked. A separate observation is that the
172.16.5.0/24 (VLAN 5) subnet returns "Destination Net Unreachable" from
the gateway for every VLAN 20 host, indicating a routing gap for that
prefix, but this is a topology-wide condition unrelated to the isolation
claim and is not the subject of this ticket. Root cause: the ticket
describes a fault that does not exist; PC11 is fully operational and
correctly connected to VLAN 20 and the rest of the campus network.
Corrective action: no remediation required — close the ticket as a
false-premise report and advise the user to retest their workstation.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes PC11 reaches its gateway 172.16.20.254, same-VLAN hosts, and off-subnet destinations with 0% loss at baseline
per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly verifies 0% packet loss from PC11 to gateway, same-VLAN peers, and off-subnet hosts, matching the baseline-healthy requirement.

The agent's investigation log contains concrete observations (pings, ip/neigh, and switch port state) that directly support the conclusion that PC11 is connected and not isolated. Minor gaps (no explicit successful pc11→pc10 ping, a timed-out pc10→pc11 attempt) are mitigated by ARP/neighbour evidence and other successful tests, so the conclusion is well supported.
